decisions.reason: “Drawing to a close” is more natural English for 마무리 단계에 접어들었다 than “entering its closing phase.”
Comma-joining the two terms is natural confirmation dialogue; the Korean period is just item listing.
틀림없소 is emphatic certainty; SOL’s “Correct” flattens it to a simple yes.
“Will sell no information” carries the contractual force of 어느 문파에게도 팔지 않을.
Preserves 밀고 당기기 as “push and pull”; SOL’s “back-and-forth” genericizes the idiom.
“Reviewed the agreement” and plural “documents” are more natural for 점검한 후 문서를 작성, 교환했다.
Em-dash on “the moment they shook hands” matches 순간이었다 interrupting into the System ding.
SOL adds “notification” to 뜨네 and drops 알림 from the second sentence.
“Joining us” is the natural in-group reading of 가세했으니 in a thought about our odds.
BASE’s “assistance” is stiff; SOL’s “invaluable” overstates 엄청난 보탬.
decisions.replacement: Wolhwa had confidently claimed that all the information in Shanxi passed through her hands. If that was true, their help would be enormous.

decisions.reason: SOL drops 달라진다 (“become anything”), 때로는 (“sometimes”), and weakens 다루느냐 from “handled” to “used.”
“It would be nice if” matches wistful 좋을 텐데; “Hopefully” is more expectant.
“I’ll be taking my leave” keeps the polite register of 이만 물러가지요; SOL is merely flatter.
BASE misreads omitted subject as Wolhwa unable to go far; SOL weakens 양해 바라오 to “I hope” and adds “so many.”
decisions.replacement: “Please understand that I cannot see you out far while there are eyes on us.”

decisions.reason: “Curved into crescents” is the natural English for 반달처럼 휘었다; “crescent moons” is redundant.
“Aren’t you going to see me off?” is more coaxing, matching teasing 안 해 줘요?
SOL specifies unsupported “ribs” for 몸 쪽 and drops 아니.
“No less” is snappier spoken English for 그것도 than “And… too.”
“A—a hot night” preserves the stutter 뜨, 뜨거운; BASE reads as repeated emphasis.
뛰쳐나가는 is “dashed out”; SOL adds unsupported “from the room.”
BASE loses the wail 야아; SOL adds unsupported “My baby.”
Naturalizes 시선이 모일 수밖에 없었다 without the double-negative “impossible not to stare.”
In-group speakers saying 가문에 naturally comes out as “our family.”
“A friend… said” is more spoken than “According to a friend.”
BASE drops 지금; SOL drops hearsay 다는.
decisions.replacement: “Ah, that Honghwaru everyone says is ridiculously expensive. I know the place. Wait, but why would a courtesan come here now?”

decisions.reason: “The Third Young Master’s unpaid tab” and “her money” are tighter and still faithful.
가지가지 is “all kinds of things,” not the more absolute “everything.”
“Wormed their way” is the English idiom; the relative clause in BASE is Korean-shaped.
떨어져 있어요 is “so far behind”; BASE adds unnecessary “walking.”
Adverb “sullenly” is cleaner English than “in a sullen tone” for 퉁명스러운 어조로.
“Ridiculous rumors” captures 헛소문; BASE’s “all kinds of rumors” misses 헛.
SOL drops 그냥 (“simply”), which marks how casually she gave the excuse.
“But why” continues the interior denial more naturally without changing 왜 하필.
전쟁이 일어난 is war having broken out, not “in the middle of a war.”
Preserves comparative 양호 and 사람들; SOL’s “everyone” overreaches.
“Sensed something off” matches 위화감을 느꼈다; SOL’s “noticed something odd” is more cognitive.
SOL flattens 협의를 조정하고 to “negotiated,” losing the fine-tuning.
빙긋 is a small smile; SOL’s plain “smiled” drops the quality.
Keeps the exclamation of 정보가! on the realization.
“Hurried to Wolhwa’s side” is more natural for 빠르게 옆으로 붙었다.
SOL drops 음모 (“conspiracy”).
그 기대 is that specific hope; SOL pluralizes to “my hopes.”
“Act according to” is the natural collocation; “move according to” sounds physical.
Spoken “Then” is tighter dialogue for 그렇다면 than “If that’s the case.”
“Stronger than us” and “shouldn’t you side” are more natural spoken English.
“Or should I say naïve?” is the English self-correction for 아니, 순진하다고 해야 하나?
피식 웃었다 is a snicker/puff; “quiet laugh” underplays it.
SOL replaces 냉정하게 (“coldly”) with “objectively,” drops 결과, and assigns unsupported “I.”
상관없다 is “it doesn’t matter”; “nothing else matters” intensifies.
확인할 수 없었다 is “couldn’t verify,” not “couldn’t uncover.”
“So well” matches 잘; BASE’s “perfectly” overstates it.
Preserves 그만큼 (“that capable”) and 그걸로 좋고 (“enough”); SOL’s “exceptionally” loses the degree.
이렇게 바라볼 수도 is “another way of looking at it,” not merely “one way.”
BASE mistranslates plural 자신들 as “herself”; SOL’s “ruthless” is not 철저한.
decisions.replacement: Thorough profit-and-loss calculation. I finally understood exactly what Wolhwa meant when she called her people merchants.

decisions.reason: Naturalizes 든든한 마음도 들었다; BASE’s “gave me a reassuring feeling” is translationese.
Restores 이 전쟁 (“this war”) and 월화도 (“even Wolhwa”).
Preserves passive 밝혀진 바가 없네요 and 최선을 다하고 (“doing its best”).
가까워진 is “approaching”; SOL’s “nearby” loses the approach.
Tension 여기까지 전해져 온다 from the carriage; SOL’s “in the air” genericizes the source.
“Channeled… into” is the natural rendering of 공력을 흘려보냈다.
귀신처럼 is “like a ghost”; SOL’s “demon” changes the image.
“Caliber” and “something else” naturalize 저 정도 and admiring 달라.
BASE mistranslates 보여 as “sounded” and intensifies 심각한 with “deadly.”
More natural spoken word order for the same question.
BASE’s “Kid” misreads 마; SOL drops 수문각, 눈빛, and “the hell.”
decisions.replacement: “Hey, this fellow and I have ten years of experience at the gate-watch office. We can tell from a person’s eyes alone. What the hell would a little shit like you know, butting into your elders’ conversation?”

decisions.reason: SOL’s 보이냐 is better, but “true masters” is unsupported; BASE’s “You call that” is looser.
decisions.replacement: “Tsk. Openings? Those look like openings to you? Can’t you see the ease and naturalness that only masters possess?”

decisions.reason: SOL fills in the interrupted 반박귀진…… with unsupported “because he’s achieved.”
SOL omits 멀뚱히 (“blankly”).
Same 귀신처럼 error as H061: “ghost,” not “demon.”
BASE drops 고수의 향기; SOL changes 묵직한 to “deep” and adds “unmistakable.”
decisions.replacement: That heavy voice. The sharp gaze that carried the air of a master.

decisions.reason: Preserves 순간 (“momentarily”) and 저 얼굴 (“that face”); SOL drops 순간.
Naturalizes calqued “crossed life and death” for 생사를 넘나들며.
“Smiled gently and opened his mouth” is more natural English word order.
SOL’s “whenever” fits 감으면, but “formidable” upgrades blunt 강한 놈.
decisions.replacement: “Even now, whenever I close my eyes, the memories of that day remain vivid. The Heavenly Axe… He was a truly strong bastard.”

decisions.reason: “Exclaimed in amazement” naturalizes stiff “let out exclamations” for 탄성을 토했다.
“The infamous” matches the specific 흉명이 자자한 figure; SOL’s extra ellipsis splits one sentence.
“Seriously wrong” is the better collocation for 대단히 잘못 알고; SOL is merely different.
“Didn’t even know” captures 지도.
“While” vs “As” is indistinguishable, so BASE.
Past counterfactual “hadn’t been” matches 아니었다면 better than “weren’t.”
Restores 참 as “certainly”; BASE drops it.
“And then” vs “then” is indistinguishable.
Fronting “when someone muttered” is natural English for the 중얼거림 that introduces the quote.
틀림없어 is “it has to be,” stronger than “it must be.”
“Someone’s mutter” already moved into H083; keeping it here would duplicate.
SOL’s “roamed” fits 주유, but “hunting down” changes 때려잡던 and drops 그 (“that”).
decisions.replacement: “Yama Whip? You mean that Peak master who roamed the realm beating down remnants of the Demonic path?”

decisions.reason: “Neither his sect nor his past known” matches 사문도, 과거도; the trail line is more natural.
해치우다 is “taking down,” not formal “defeating”; “And not only that” keeps 그뿐인가.
BASE adds “admiring”; SOL overstates 는지 as “must have” and 붙들고 as “clamped.”
decisions.replacement: Fervent gazes poured in from every direction. Perhaps sensing that something was wrong, the coachman tried to pull away, but my hand was gripping his shoulder tightly.

decisions.reason: Preserves 염.라.편. 대협 order and 다시 뵙는군요; SOL reorders the title and adds “To think we would.”
“Like oil thrown onto a fire” is the natural idiom for 불길에 기름을 끼얹는.
달아오른 is “overheated/fired up,” not generic “excited”; 허리를 숙였다 is “bent over,” not “doubled over.”
“Came to mind” is the natural collocation for 떠올렸다.
빛을 잃었고 is light gone out/lost, not the softer “faded.”
BASE leaves whose skin unclear; SOL’s “fierce” is not 강렬한.
decisions.replacement: A large, rough hand caressed the young man’s face. Intense poisonous energy seeped through the man’s skin, only to be stopped by the internal energy that instinctively surged within him.

decisions.reason: 한탄했다 is “lamented,” not the broader “mourned.”
Preserves 자라 (“grown up”) and 천애 고아 (“complete orphan”); SOL drops the growing-up.
Keeps 많은/많은 repetition, 풋내기 as “green,” and does not add “accumulated.”
원통 is dying wronged/unjustly, not merely “bitter.”
BASE drops 실핏줄 (“tiny”); SOL drops 가만히 (“quietly”).
decisions.replacement: He quietly looked down at his son’s wide-open eyes. Every tiny blood vessel had burst, staining the irises red.

decisions.reason: BASE’s “He” is ambiguous; SOL’s “bloody tears” and “child” weaken 피눈물 and 아들.
decisions.replacement: His son was barely twenty. Blood tears flowed from the eyes of a father who stood before his poisoned son.

decisions.reason: “Entire” vs “whole” is indistinguishable.
“I will” matches the solemn vow 하마; “I’ll” is too casual.
강대한 is “powerful,” not “immense”; “rose like a wildfire” and “had been consuming” match 일어나 and 잠식해 가던.
“Hundredfold. A thousandfold” matches 백배 천배로, and “I will” matches 하마.
시신을 뒤로하고 걸었다 is “left behind and walked,” not “turned his back” and “strode.”
“Flickering torches” matches the noun phrase 일렁이는 횃불들 more cleanly.
Keeps 무리 (“a group of”) and 고개를 숙였다 (“bowed his head”).
“Nodded to” is the acknowledgment/permission nod before 가라.
“Our revenge begins” is stronger vow English with the same meaning as 복수의 시작이다.
빠져나왔다 is plain “left,” not formal “departed.”
